At secondary and superior lvl, NC acts like a sensdep, but with a
significant change other than the lower blood cost.

"the minion with this card does not untap as normal"

Sensdep specifies "as normal during the untap phase", so does NC
therefore restrict the minion from using untaps like rats warning,
metro underground, masikas special, etc.?

Or was the card meant to include the secondary text above "during the
untap phase". Otherwise, I would read it as restricting the vamp from
auxilliary untaps like above.

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
In message <3c24facf.82971962@news>,
Talo...@nospam.hotmail.com mumbled something about:

>At secondary and superior lvl, NC acts like a sensdep, but with a
>significant change other than the lower blood cost.

The superior includes "tap that minion", making it marginally stronger
than Sensory Deprivation. It is worth noting that no vampire currently
in the game possesses both superior Auspex and superior Chimerstry.

>"the minion with this card does not untap as normal"
>
>Sensdep specifies "as normal during the untap phase", so does NC
>therefore restrict the minion from using untaps like rats warning,
>metro underground, masikas special, etc.?

All the effects you list are not "normal" untaps. There is only one
"normal" time a minion untaps -- during the untap phase. So NC does not
restrict Rat's Warning, Majesty, or any other untap effects.

Things like Rat's Warning are "abnormal" untaps, as they are specific
card effects that override the rules. Sensory Deprivation's additional
text dates from Dark Sovereigns and is redundant (although it confirms
that the untap phase is, indeed, the "normal" time to untap).

To achieve the effect you are thinking of, we look at inferior Sleeping
Mind, which restricts inferior Cat's Guidance, Majesty, Earth Meld,
Rat's Warning, and a number of other cards:

"[DOM] Only usable when the acting vampire's action is announced.
Minions cannot untap during this action."

...Note the lack of "as normal" in the text.
